title: How HTTPS Keeps Your Data Private

narration: Imagine you press Submit on a login form.
A watcher sits on the path.
What does it see?
beats.visual_intent: One light board: a browser card on the left with a login form and a Submit button, a server card on the right, a path between them with a router box and a watcher marker on it. On Submit, a packet carrying the readable form fields leaves the browser along the path.

grounding.claim: A form submission crosses the path with a watcher on it (illustrative)

narration: Plain web traffic is readable text.
Anyone on the path can copy it.
beats.visual_intent: The packet passes the watcher, which duplicates it; the copy shows the same readable form fields, held beside the original so both read identically.

grounding.claim: Plain HTTP traffic is readable text
Anyone on the path can read it

narration: Follow this request, and see why it turns to noise.
beats.visual_intent: The same board holds still; a small open padlock icon appears above the path, promising the outcome, without changing the layout.

grounding.claim: Promise of the lesson's outcome: the padlock and what it protects

narration: The browser asks the server to identify itself.
It sends a certificate, signed by an authority.
beats.visual_intent: A request arrow runs from browser to server; a certificate card slides back to the browser showing a domain name and a key, and an authority seal appears on the words 'signed by'.

grounding.claim: A certificate ties a domain name to a public key and is signed by a certificate authority

narration: The browser checks three things:
signer trusted, name matches, in date.
beats.visual_intent: On the certificate card at the browser, three ticks appear one at a time beside signer, name and dates, each on its phrase.

grounding.claim: Browser checks that the signature chains to a trusted authority, the name matches and the certificate is within its dates

narration: Next, both ends need a shared key.
In modern HTTPS, it is never sent.
beats.visual_intent: The certificate card shrinks to a ticked badge; an empty key slot appears at each end of the path, with the watcher still between them.

grounding.claim: In modern HTTPS the shared session key is agreed without being sent across the network

narration: Each side sends a temporary value.
The watcher copies both,
yet cannot practically work out the key.
beats.visual_intent: Two small value tokens cross the path in opposite directions; the watcher copies each into a tray, and a blank key slot stays empty beside the watcher.

grounding.claim: Each side contributes a temporary value and they combine them into the shared key
A watcher who records every value cannot practically work out the key

narration: Both ends reach the same key.
beats.visual_intent: Matching keys appear in the slots at browser and server only; the watcher's slot remains empty.

grounding.claim: Both ends reach the same session key
Watcher cannot practically work out the key

narration: Those checks are why the key is trusted.
Name them.
beats.visual_intent: The ticked badge enlarges beside the keys and its three ticks re-light in turn, tying the key to the passed check.

recall.answer: Signer trusted, name matches, in date.

grounding.claim: Server signs the key agreement with its certificate's key, so an impostor fails the checks

narration: HTTPS is that request inside a protected channel.
The key scrambles the form.
beats.visual_intent: The form data block at the browser, readable, passes through the key and turns into scrambled blocks as it leaves.

grounding.claim: HTTPS is the same web request carried inside a protected TLS channel
The shared key scrambles the data at one end and unscrambles it at the other
Form contents such as a password travel as scrambled bytes

narration: The watcher copies the bytes,
but cannot read them.
beats.visual_intent: Scrambled blocks travel past the watcher, whose copy is the same unreadable pattern.

grounding.claim: A watcher can copy the scrambled bytes but cannot read them

narration: The server unscrambles it with the same key.
beats.visual_intent: At the server the scrambled blocks pass the key and turn readable again.

grounding.claim: The same key unscrambles the data at the far end
